title: Interoperability of "scroll to fragment" timing
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

This comes from a discussion with @kojiishi after the F2F, where I proposed that "scroll to the fragment identifier" is something pretty similar to what they are trying to do for auto-resizing iframes ([here](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1771#issuecomment-3806716273)).

It seems browsers do fairly different things for when to [scroll to the fragment identifier](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier), so probably we want to do something simpler / easier / more consistent for that auto-resizing iframe feature, but still it seems worth aligning here or at least getting discussion going.

Gecko's implementation ([`Document::ScrollToRef()`](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/search?q=symbol:_ZN7mozilla3dom8Document11ScrollToRefEv&redirect=false)) happens:

 * When parser-inserted stylesheets have finished loading.
 * When the XML-parser is interrupted (not sure when that happens, @hsivonen do you know?)
 * From some navigation API stuff (`NavigateEvent::ProcessScrollBehavior`)
 * On the initial page layout (`nsDocumentViewer::InitPresentationStuff`)
 * On load (`nsDocumentViewer::LoadComplete`)

Blink's implementation, quoting @kojiishi:

> In Blink, [FragmentAnchor::Invoke()](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/fragment_directive/selector_fragment_anchor.cc;l=29;bpv=1;bpt=1?q=FragmentAnchor::Invoke&ss=chromium%2Fchromium%2Fsrc) is called from [Document::UpdateStyleAndLayout()](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/document.cc;l=3058?q=Document::UpdateStyleAndLayout&ss=chromium%2Fchromium%2Fsrc). The step runs after every layout, determining whether it should actually scroll or not from various states.

WebKit's impl is [here](https://searchfox.org/wubkat/search?q=symbol:_ZN7WebCore14LocalFrameView16scrollToFragmentERKN3WTF3URLE&redirect=false). From a bit of code inspection I think it is roughly:

 * When all the parser inserted stylesheets have finished loading
 * The same NavigateEvent stuff that Gecko has (`NavigateEvent::processScrollBehavior`)
 * When drawing SVG images.
 * On DOMContentLoaded I think? (FrameLoader::finishedParsing)
 * On same-document navigations (FrameLoader::loadInSameDocument)

It seems Gecko's and WebKit's implementations are fairly close.

This seems the kind of thing that could be better specified, if only so authors have a good sense of when is it safe to mutate the page if they want their anchors to work properly?

Would other browsers be willing to align behaviors here? The current state seems quite messy, and this is pretty observable.

/cc @kojiishi @bfgeek @smaug---- @jnjaeschke @rniwa @annevk
